gen-fs-quilon-gf-julius-sans-one: Commanding yet editorial, Quilon swells and thins in a measured rhythm, with generous openings in its tall a, e and s. And Julius Sans One stays hairline-plain beneath it, its capitals nearly level with the lowercase and its curves left wide open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, its lowercase sitting tall with a gaping c. Quilon above it adds a slight tug of heavier verticals, so a long stretch of text feels sturdy and approachable, never fussy or thin.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-kedebideri: Approachable from the first glance. Quilon does its best work with a mild stroke contrast and editorial confidence, while Kedebideri is happiest as a sans with a skyward x-height and rounded, inviting curves.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-khula: Quilon leads with a soft cadence of fuller stems and slimmer links. Its strongest quality is how that gentle swing sits against Khula, a plain sans with a tall midsection and curves that keep their mouths open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-krub: Tall, confident, editorial: Quilon sets that tone with a modest weight shift across every curve. But Krub, with its pronounced x-height and pen-lifted curves, keeps a longer passage moving lightly without ever feeling heavy.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-kufam: Kufam draws one uniform line, like a neon sign tube. Quilon beside it brings a faint but real thick-thin shift, so the heading feels shaped by a hand while the body stays flat, open and plainly spoken.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend: Quilon is editorial and commanding, its curves thinning modestly wherever they turn, set above a body with a different temperament. Lexend answers in a single-weight line, like a plotter pen, and the two stay clearly apart.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-deca: Commanding, shaded display letters up top, with large open counters in its a, e and s. Lexend Deca follows in a plain, unshaded line, so go generous on the heading and modest below.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-exa: A calm ebb and flow of stroke thickness defines Quilon, giving it a commanding editorial presence. Lexend Exa counters by holding one thickness in every direction, with wide curves that stay distinct and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-giga: Quilon brings an editorial, commanding voice, with a gentle weight change where its bowls curve around. Lexend Giga then reads in flat, single-weight lines with generous tracking, so a long passage moves openly, one word at a time.
